{{Short description|Group theoretic operation}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Rosati involution''', named after [[Carlo Rosati]],  is an involution of the rational [[endomorphism ring]] of an [[abelian variety]] induced by a [[Abelian_variety#Polarisations|polarisation]].

Let <math>A</math> be an [[abelian variety]], let <math>\hat{A} = \mathrm{Pic}^0(A)</math> be the [[dual abelian variety]], and for <math>a\in A</math>, let <math>T_a:A\to A</math> be the translation-by-<math>a</math> map, <math>T_a(x)=x+a</math>. Then each divisor <math>D</math> on <math>A</math> defines a map <math>\phi_D:A\to\hat A</math> via <math>\phi_D(a)=[T_a^*D-D]</math>.  The map <math>\phi_D</math> is a polarisation if <math>D</math> is [[ample divisor|ample]].  The Rosati involution of <math>\mathrm{End}(A)\otimes\mathbb{Q}</math> relative to the polarisation  <math>\phi_D</math> sends a map <math>\psi\in\mathrm{End}(A)\otimes\mathbb{Q}</math> to the map <math>\psi'=\phi_D^{-1}\circ\hat\psi\circ\phi_D</math>, where <math>\hat\psi:\hat A\to\hat A</math> is the dual map induced by the action of <math>\psi^*</math> on <math>\mathrm{Pic}(A)</math>.

Let <math>\mathrm{NS}(A)</math> denote the [[Néron–Severi group]] of <math>A</math>. The polarisation <math>\phi_D</math> also induces an inclusion <math>\Phi:\mathrm{NS}(A)\otimes\mathbb{Q}\to\mathrm{End}(A)\otimes\mathbb{Q}</math> via <math>\Phi_E=\phi_D^{-1}\circ\phi_E</math>. The image of <math>\Phi</math> is equal to <math>\{\psi\in\mathrm{End}(A)\otimes\mathbb{Q}:\psi'=\psi\}</math>, i.e., the set of endomorphisms fixed by the Rosati involution.  The operation <math>E\star F=\frac12\Phi^{-1}(\Phi_E\circ\Phi_F+\Phi_F\circ\Phi_E)</math> then gives <math>\mathrm{NS}(A)\otimes\mathbb{Q}</math> the structure of a formally real [[Jordan algebra]].
